definitions.explanation: The official language of a country.
The subject of Japanese language arts in school.

examples.japanese: {国語|こくご}の{授業|じゅぎょう}
{国語|こくご}が{得意|とくい}だ。
{日本|にほん}の{国語|こくご}は{日本語|にほんご}だ。
その{国|くに}には{二|ふた}つの{国語|こくご}がある。
examples.english: That country has two national languages.

examples.japanese: カナダでは{英語|えいご}とフランス{語|ご}の{二|ふた}つが{国語|こくご}として{定|さだ}められている。
examples.english: In Canada, English and French are established as the two national languages.

notes:
{国語|こくご} means "national language." In Japan, this specifically refers to the Japanese language, especially as a school subject.

COMMON COMPOUNDS:
- {国語|こくご}{辞典|じてん}: Japanese-language dictionary
- {国語|こくご}の{教科書|きょうかしょ}: Japanese textbook
- {国語|こくご}の{授業|じゅぎょう}: Japanese language class
- {国語|こくご}{力|りょく}: Japanese language ability

AS A SCHOOL SUBJECT:
{国語|こくご} is one of the core subjects in Japanese education, covering reading, writing, grammar, and literature. It is equivalent to "Language Arts" or "English" class in English-speaking countries.

CONTRAST:
- {国語|こくご}: Japanese as a native language/school subject
- {日本語|にほんご}: Japanese language (used when talking about it as a foreign language or linguistically)
- {英語|えいご}: English (as a school subject: {英語|えいご}の{授業|じゅぎょう})
